messages.content: How much electricity will I need for my 2000 sq ft home?

function.name: solar_panel_calculate_need

message.content:
A good rule‑of‑thumb for U.S. residential electricity use is **about 5 kWh per square foot per year** for a typical, reasonably insulated home in a moderate climate. That translates to roughly:

| Square footage | Annual kWh (≈5 kWh/ft²) | Daily kWh |
|----------------|------------------------|-----------|
| 2,000 ft²      | ~10,000 kWh            | ~27 kWh   |

### Why the number varies

| Factor | Effect on consumption |
|--------|-----------------------|
| **Climate** | Hot climates (air‑conditioning) or cold climates (heating) can push usage up to 7–8 kWh/ft²/year. |
| **Insulation & windows** | Poor insulation or many single‑pane windows can add 1–2 kWh/ft²/year. |
| **Appliances & electronics** | High‑efficiency appliances reduce usage; a lot of electronics or a home office can increase it. |
| **Occupancy** | More occupants → more lights, water heating, etc. |
| **Energy‑saving habits** | Turning off lights, using smart thermostats, etc., can shave off 10–20 %. |

### Rough ranges

| Climate / Efficiency | Annual kWh (2,000 ft²) |
|----------------------|------------------------|
| Mild, well‑insulated | 8,000–10,000 kWh |
| Moderate, average | 10,000–12,000 kWh |
| Hot or cold, less efficient | 12,000–15,000 kWh |

So, for a 2,000 sq ft home, you can expect to use somewhere between **8,000 and 15,000 kWh per year**, depending on the factors above. If you’d like a more precise estimate tailored to your specific climate, insulation, and appliance mix—or if you’re curious about how many solar panels you’d need to cover that load—just let me know!
